problem.title: Connection problem · {{name}}
problem.ipFromServer: The server says you connected from {{ip}} (unverified: “See my public IP” confirms it).

firewall.title: The server's firewall blocks your IP
firewall.azure: Azure SQL only accepts connections from the IPs allowed in the server's firewall, and yours isn't one of them. Add it as a rule and connect again (the change can take a few minutes).
firewall.other: The server doesn't accept connections from your address. Ask for your public IP to be allowed (for example in pg_hba.conf, the MySQL user's allowed hosts or the server's firewall).

timeout.title: The server didn't answer
timeout.body: The connection didn't reach the server in time. Most often:

refused.title: The server refused the connection
refused.body: The machine was reached but nothing is listening on that port, or there's no route to it. Most often:

dns.title: The server can't be found
dns.body: The name {{host}} doesn't resolve. Check that it's spelled right and, if it's an internal name, that you're on the network or VPN that resolves it.

tls.title: The secure connection (TLS) failed
tls.body: The server's certificate isn't trusted or doesn't match the host name. Check the connection's encryption options: use the name on the certificate, or trust the server's certificate only if you know it's the right one.

auth.title: Login rejected
auth.body: The server rejected the user or password. Check the credentials and the authentication method (for example Microsoft Entra), and that the user exists in that database.

unknown.title: Couldn't connect
unknown.body: The server or the driver answered with this message.

network.vpn: The VPN to the server's network isn't connected.
network.firewall: A firewall on the way (an Azure NSG or WAF, the virtual machine's firewall or your network's) drops traffic to port {{port}}.
network.down: The server or the service is stopped, or listens on another port.
network.azureVm: {{host}} is an Azure virtual machine: SQL Server runs on the VM, so the rule goes in its NSG or WAF (or the VM's Windows firewall), not in the Azure SQL firewall.
network.azureSql: With Azure SQL, an IP that isn't allowed gets a firewall error, not a timeout: if it doesn't answer, check that your network lets port 1433 out.

azure.add: Add my IP to the Azure firewall
azure.confirmTitle: This rule will be created in your Azure account
azure.confirmNote: It's a change to the Azure SQL server's firewall, made with your Azure CLI (az) session.
azure.prodConfirm: This is a production connection. Type “{{name}}” to confirm:
azure.created: Rule {{rule}} created on {{server}} (group {{group}}) for {{ip}}. It can take a few minutes to apply: then, Retry.
azure.azMissing: The Azure CLI (az) wasn't found on this machine. You can create the rule in one of these ways:
azure.azLoggedOut: The Azure CLI (az) isn't logged in (run “az login” and try again). Meanwhile, you can create the rule in one of these ways:
azure.byCli: With the Azure CLI (fill in the resource group):
azure.byPortal: In the Azure portal: the server › Networking › Firewall rules › Add your client IP.
azure.byTsql: With T-SQL, from another connection that does have access, in the master database:
azure.unavailable: Azure reports the database isn't available right now (it happens while it's moved or scaled). Wait a minute and retry.
azure.ipVerified: your public IP, verified over HTTPS

problem.ipMismatch: The server reported a different IP ({{server}}): it doesn't match your public IP, so it isn't used.
